cues.en: Instructor: The correlation coefficient is a really fundamental and ubiquitous analysis.
cues.zh: 講師：相關係數是一種非常基礎，而且無所不在的分析。

cues.en: It is present all throughout statistics, all throughout machine learning, all throughout deep learning.
cues.zh: 整個統計學、機器學習與深度學習領域，都會用到它。

cues.en: You basically see it all over the place.
cues.zh: 基本上到處都看得到。

cues.en: Correlation is everywhere.
cues.zh: 相關無所不在。

cues.en: So in this section I'm gonna teach you all sorts of crazy interesting things about correlations, regular correlations, covariance, partial correlations,
cues.zh: 因此，在本單元我會教你各種非常有趣的相關概念，包括一般相關、共變異數、偏相關，

cues.en: non-parametric correlations, and so on.
cues.zh: 無母數相關等等。

cues.en: And I'm going to start the section in this video by just explaining a bit of the motivation, the logic behind correlation analysis.
cues.zh: 本單元就從這支影片開始，先解釋相關分析的動機與背後邏輯。

cues.en: And I will give some examples of what correlations do and do not reveal about the underlying data.
cues.zh: 我也會舉例說明，相關能揭露、以及不能揭露底層資料的哪些特性。

cues.en: So far, you've learned about t-tests, and there we are considering the average of one group against the average of another group.
cues.zh: 目前你已經學過 t 檢定，當時比較的是一組平均值與另一組平均值。

cues.en: And in this case, what we are actually doing is ignoring individual differences.
cues.zh: 在那種情況下，我們其實忽略了個體差異。

cues.en: So let's imagine each of these circles here represents a different person.
cues.zh: 假設這裡每個圓圈代表不同的人。

cues.en: These are people in group A, and these are people in group B.
cues.zh: 這些人是 A 組，這些人是 B 組。

cues.en: So we actually ignore all of the individual variability.
cues.zh: 我們其實忽略了所有個體變異。

cues.en: We pretend like everyone in this group is the same and everyone in this group is the same.
cues.zh: 假裝這一組每個人都一樣，另一組每個人也都一樣。

cues.en: And the question is whether these homogenous robots are different from these homogenous robots.
cues.zh: 問題就變成：這群同質的機器人，與另一群同質的機器人是否不同？

cues.en: So this is kind of a problem in apology quotes here because it's a bug or a feature of the t-test, but regardless of how you think of it,
cues.zh: 這算是一個加上引號的「問題」，因為它可能是 t 檢定的缺點，也可能是特性；但無論你怎麼看，

cues.en: the t-test and other measures of group differences, including ANOVA's that you'll learn about in the next section, they completely ignore individual differences.
cues.zh: t 檢定與其他衡量組間差異的方法，包括下一單元會學到的 ANOVA，都完全忽略個體差異。

cues.en: But of course, you know from your experience as a human that people are different.
cues.zh: 但身為人類，你當然從經驗知道，每個人都不同。

cues.en: Different people are different from each other.
cues.zh: 不同的人彼此不一樣。

cues.en: So the T-test completely ignores all of that individual variability but we need a set of methods that can highlight,
cues.zh: t 檢定完全忽略了這些個體變異，但我們需要一套方法，能凸顯，

cues.en: that can capture that individual variability, focus on that individual variability and reveal whether there are some important relationships
cues.zh: 捕捉並聚焦在個體變異，揭露個體變異與其他變數之間，

cues.en: between individual variability and some other variable.
cues.zh: 是否存在某些重要關係。

cues.en: Okay, so that is the idea of a correlation.
cues.zh: 這就是相關的概念。

cues.en: So now let's imagine that instead of considering these to be homogenous blocks of goop, we are thinking about these as being unique individuals
cues.zh: 現在我們不再把這些人看成同質的一團東西，而是把他們當作獨特的個體，

cues.en: with all their own specific personalities and interests and tastes and behavioral patterns, and so on.
cues.zh: 各有自己的個性、興趣、喜好、行為模式等等。

cues.en: So we're gonna label these.
cues.zh: 所以我們替他們編號。

cues.en: This is person one, person two, and so on.
cues.zh: 這是第 1 個人、第 2 個人，以此類推。

cues.en: We have nine of them here and nine of them in this group.
cues.zh: 這邊有 9 個人，這一組也有 9 個人。

cues.en: Now I'm labeling these one and one and two and two because to compute a correlation, you need to have data that are paired somehow.
cues.zh: 我把這裡標成 1 和 1、2 和 2，是因為計算相關時，資料必須具有某種配對關係。

cues.en: They don't need to be exactly the same individual.
cues.zh: 不一定非得是同一個人。

cues.en: So this doesn't need to be the same person as this one, but this number one and this number one need to be somehow related to each other in a meaningful way
cues.zh: 這個人不一定要與這個人相同，但這個 1 與這個 1，必須以某種有意義的方式彼此關聯，

cues.en: because we also need to compute this person two and this person two, this person three and this person three.
cues.zh: 因為我們也必須對應這個 2 與這個 2、這個 3 與這個 3。

cues.en: Now these don't have to be different people, these can also be different measures within the same person.
cues.zh: 這些也不一定是不同的人，也可以是同一個人的不同量測。

cues.en: So let's imagine that we have nine different individuals.
cues.zh: 假設我們有 9 位不同的個體。

cues.en: So one and one do correspond to the same individual, but we're measuring different things from the same individual.
cues.zh: 1 和 1 確實對應同一個人，但量測這個人的不同項目。

cues.en: So maybe this is your score on a history exam.
cues.zh: 例如這是你歷史考試的成績。

cues.en: And so the blue circles are your scores on history exam and this is your scores on a programming exam.
cues.zh: 藍色圓圈是歷史考試成績，這邊則是程式設計考試成績。

cues.en: And we want to know do people who do well in history also tend to do well in a coding course?
cues.zh: 我們想知道，歷史表現好的人，程式設計課是否也通常表現較好？

cues.en: So you can still see, so these can be the same individuals or different individuals, but they do need to be paired, they need to be related to each other somehow.
cues.zh: 因此，這些可以是同一批人，也可以是不同的人，但必須配對，彼此具有某種關係。

cues.en: So I'm gonna do a thought experiment here and I've never really been a fan of death metal music.
cues.zh: 這裡做個思想實驗。我一直不太喜歡死亡金屬音樂。

cues.en: Do you like death metal music?
cues.zh: 你喜歡死亡金屬嗎？

cues.en: So I wonder if the appreciation of death metal music has a genetic component.
cues.zh: 我想知道，喜歡死亡金屬這件事是否有遺傳成分。

cues.en: If there's something in our genes that make us like or dislike death metal music.
cues.zh: 我們的基因裡，是否有什麼因素讓我們喜歡或不喜歡死亡金屬？

cues.en: So I'm gonna do a thought experiment.
cues.zh: 所以我做一個思想實驗。

cues.en: I'm gonna go around the world, find these identical twins who were separated at birth.
cues.zh: 到世界各地，尋找出生時就分開的同卵雙胞胎。

cues.en: There's not many of them, but they do exist, identical twins who were separated at birth.
cues.zh: 這種人不多，但確實存在出生時就分開的同卵雙胞胎。

cues.en: It's pretty interesting.
cues.zh: 這很有意思。

cues.en: There's been a bunch of research on these twins.
cues.zh: 有人對這些雙胞胎做過很多研究。

cues.en: You can look it up, it's pretty remarkable how similar they are.
cues.zh: 你可以查一查，他們相似的程度相當驚人。

cues.en: So I'm gonna find these twins and I'm just going to ask them how much they like death metal music, let's say on a scale from one to 10.
cues.zh: 我要找到這些雙胞胎，詢問他們有多喜歡死亡金屬，假設用 1 到 10 分評分。

cues.en: So here I have nine different twins who are identical separated at birth.
cues.zh: 這裡有 9 組出生時就分開的同卵雙胞胎。

cues.en: So this is one pair of twins, nine, where's nine, nine and nine are another pair of twins.
cues.zh: 這是一對雙胞胎，9 在哪裡？9 和 9 是另一對。

cues.en: And we ask them this question.
cues.zh: 我們問他們這個問題。

cues.en: So we can plot the data and it's going to look something like this for this group.
cues.zh: 把資料畫出來，這一組可能像這樣。

cues.en: So this is a y-axis drawn here, but this would be how much you like death metal music.
cues.zh: 這裡畫的是 Y 軸，表示你有多喜歡死亡金屬音樂。

cues.en: So you know, person one, three, five, and nine, they don't really like death metal music.
cues.zh: 第 1、3、5 和 9 個人不太喜歡死亡金屬。

cues.en: Six and seven, they like death metal music a lot.
cues.zh: 第 6 和第 7 個人很喜歡。

cues.en: And you know, two and eight, they feel sort of lukewarm about death metal music.
cues.zh: 第 2 和第 8 個人對死亡金屬則沒有特別熱衷，也不太排斥。

cues.en: And then we go and we find their twins and we say, how much do you like death metal music?
cues.zh: 接著找到他們各自的雙胞胎手足，問他們有多喜歡死亡金屬。

cues.en: And then we can plot those.
cues.zh: 然後也把結果畫出來。

cues.en: So then, what you see, it doesn't really matter whether group one or group two is higher, we don't really care about that for the correlation.
cues.zh: 這裡第一組還是第二組的分數較高，其實不重要；相關分析不關心這一點。

cues.en: What we care about is whether these two groups are going up and down together.
cues.zh: 我們關心的是，這兩組是否一起上升、一起下降。

cues.en: So the fact that both twos are higher than both ones, the threes are lower, the fours are higher.
cues.zh: 例如兩個 2 都比兩個 1 高，兩個 3 較低，兩個 4 較高。

cues.en: So these are all relative.
cues.zh: 所以這些都是相對的。

cues.en: So we want to know, are these twins basically, do they have similar preferences relative to other twins in this group?
cues.zh: 我們想知道的是：相較於這一組中的其他雙胞胎，這些雙胞胎彼此是否有類似的偏好？

cues.en: So you can also see here that the correlation is something that we define over a group.
cues.zh: 這裡也可以看出，相關是針對一組資料定義的。

cues.en: It's not possible to compute a correlation coefficient on one pair of data points.
cues.zh: 無法只憑一對資料點計算相關係數。

cues.en: So in this case, an identical twin.
cues.zh: 在這個例子中，就是一對同卵雙胞胎。

cues.en: Or if we are measuring the relationship between history exams and programming exams, you cannot measure that correlation in one person just from one exam.
cues.zh: 若量測歷史考試與程式設計考試之間的關係，也不能只憑一個人一次考試的結果來量測相關。

cues.en: So you need multiple data points.
cues.zh: 因此需要多個資料點。

cues.en: Now this way of plotting the data is this is one way of plotting the data, but this doesn't actually reveal the correlation.
cues.zh: 這種畫法是呈現資料的一種方式，但實際上還沒把相關呈現出來。

cues.en: To reveal the correlation, we actually put their preferences both on the axes.
cues.zh: 要呈現相關，必須把雙方的偏好分別放在兩條座標軸上。

cues.en: So we draw new axes that looks like this.
cues.zh: 因此我們畫一組新的座標軸，像這樣。

cues.en: So this is how much does twin number one like death metal.
cues.zh: 這是雙胞胎中的第 1 位有多喜歡死亡金屬。

cues.en: And this the y-axis here is how much does twin number two like death metal.
cues.zh: 這裡的 Y 軸則是第 2 位有多喜歡死亡金屬。

cues.en: So now we can take each individual pair.
cues.zh: 現在取出每一對雙胞胎。

cues.en: So now this data point here actually corresponds to a pair of individuals, it's not one person, it's pair number one, so it's two people.
cues.zh: 這個資料點其實對應一對個體，不是一個人，而是第 1 對，也就是兩個人。

cues.en: This is how much twin one likes death metal and this is how much twin two likes death metal in pair one and so on.
cues.zh: 這是第 1 對中第一位喜歡死亡金屬的程度，這是第二位喜歡的程度，依此類推。

cues.en: And now what you see is there's a pretty clear line between these.
cues.zh: 現在可以看到，這些點之間有一條相當明顯的直線。

cues.en: So this supports my bizarre hypothesis that there's something genetic, there's something built into our brains that makes us like or not like death metal music.
cues.zh: 因此，這支持了我那個古怪的假設：有某種遺傳因素、某種內建於腦中的因素，讓我們喜歡或不喜歡死亡金屬。

cues.en: Okay, so with this in mind, now I'm going to start to give some more formal definitions and descriptions and then we'll start getting into the math
cues.zh: 有了這個概念，現在開始給一些更正式的定義與說明，下一支影片再進入

cues.en: in the next video.
cues.zh: 數學部分。

cues.en: So here's a bunch of text and let's go through it one by one.
cues.zh: 這裡有不少文字，我們逐一說明。

cues.en: So a correlation analysis, the goal of a correlation analysis is to compute a correlation coefficient.
cues.zh: 相關分析的目標，是計算相關係數。

cues.en: That's what it's called.
cues.zh: 它就叫這個名字。

cues.en: It's called a coefficient, correlation coefficient.
cues.zh: 叫作係數，相關係數。

cues.en: It's usually termed r, I don't know why that's the case, but it's usually given the letter r.
cues.zh: 通常用 r 表示；我不知道原因，但通常指定字母 r。

cues.en: So the correlation coefficient r is a single number.
cues.zh: 相關係數 r 是單一數值。

cues.en: It is one number and it shows the linear relationship between two variables.
cues.zh: 它是一個數字，表示兩個變數之間的線性關係。

cues.en: And I'll talk more about what this means for there to be a linear relationship later in this video and then again throughout this section.
cues.zh: 稍後在本影片，以及本單元其他地方，會進一步說明線性關係的意思。

cues.en: So a correlation coefficient is standardized, it varies from minus one to plus one.
cues.zh: 相關係數經過標準化，範圍從負 1 到正 1。

cues.en: Minus one means a perfect inverse relationship.
cues.zh: 負 1 表示完全的反向關係。

cues.en: So one variable goes up, the other variable goes down, plus one means a perfect positive relationship, so they both go up and down together.
cues.zh: 一個變數上升，另一個就下降；正 1 表示完全的正向關係，兩者一起上升、一起下降。

cues.en: And a correlation coefficient of zero means no relationship.
cues.zh: 相關係數為 0，表示沒有關係。

cues.en: So knowing something about one variable doesn't tell you anything about the other variable.
cues.zh: 也就是知道其中一個變數的資訊，並不能告訴你另一個變數的任何資訊。

cues.en: And the last point on this slide is that the correlation coefficient is a continuous measure of correlation strength.
cues.zh: 這張投影片的最後一點是，相關係數是衡量相關強度的連續指標。

cues.en: That means that we cannot just look at a correlation value and determine without any other context whether that is meaningful or not meaningful.
cues.zh: 也就是不能光看一個相關值，不考慮其他背景，就判定它有沒有意義。

cues.en: You cannot say, well the r equals 0.2, so therefore it's significant or it's big.
cues.zh: 不能說 r 等於 0.2，所以它就是顯著的，或是很大。

cues.en: So you need to compute a corresponding p-value that accompanies each r value.
cues.zh: 你需要計算每個 r 值對應的 P 值。

cues.en: And the p-value is what you use to interpret the statistical significance.
cues.zh: 再用 P 值解讀統計顯著性。

cues.en: Of course, I will show you how to compute this p-value in a later video.
cues.zh: 後面的影片當然會示範如何計算這個 P 值。

cues.en: Okay, so I want to get back to this idea of positive and negative relationships with some graphical examples.
cues.zh: 現在回到正向與負向關係的概念，用幾張圖舉例。

cues.en: So here we have a positive correlation.
cues.zh: 這裡是正相關。

cues.en: You can see that when one variable goes up, the other variable also goes up.
cues.zh: 可以看到，一個變數上升，另一個變數也上升。

cues.en: So there are axes here, which I don't draw.
cues.zh: 這裡有座標軸，只是我沒有畫出來。

cues.en: So when twin one likes death metal more, then twin two also likes death metal more.
cues.zh: 當雙胞胎中的第一位更喜歡死亡金屬，第二位也更喜歡。

cues.en: Here we have a negative relationship.
cues.zh: 這裡是負向關係。

cues.en: So one variable goes up and the other variable goes down.
cues.zh: 一個變數上升，另一個變數下降。

cues.en: So x is getting larger, y is getting smaller, this is a negative correlation, it's going down, positive correlations go up.
cues.zh: X 愈來愈大，Y 愈來愈小，這就是負相關，往下走；正相關則往上走。

cues.en: And then we can have a zero correlation.
cues.zh: 也可能是零相關。

cues.en: This means that there is no relationship.
cues.zh: 意思是沒有關係。

cues.en: This is actually a little bit analogous to the concept of conditional probability that you learned about a while ago.
cues.zh: 這其實有點類似前面學過的條件機率概念。

cues.en: So when the conditional probability is zero or doesn't add anything, then you say that no information about variable x
cues.zh: 當條件機率為 0，或沒有增加任何資訊時，我們就說，變數 X 的資訊

cues.en: tells us about variable y.
cues.zh: 無法告訴我們變數 Y 的情況。

cues.en: So that's like a zero correlation.
cues.zh: 這就類似零相關。

cues.en: Now you have to be a little bit careful with the terminology here.
cues.zh: 不過這裡的用語要稍微小心。

cues.en: Sometimes people will say that there is no correlation between these two variables.
cues.zh: 有時人們會說，這兩個變數之間沒有相關。

cues.en: In fact, that is not a sensible thing to say, it never happens that there is no correlation because there's always a correlation between two variables,
cues.zh: 其實這樣說不太合理，因為兩個變數之間總有一個相關值，不會完全沒有相關，

cues.en: but that correlation coefficient can be zero or very close to zero and not statistically significantly different from zero.
cues.zh: 只是相關係數可能為 0，或非常接近 0，而且與 0 的差異未達統計顯著。

cues.en: So when people often, when people say no correlation, they're typically what they really mean typically is zero correlation.
cues.zh: 所以當人們說「沒有相關」時，通常真正的意思是「零相關」。

cues.en: Now of course there's worse mistakes you can make in life than calling zero correlation no correlation, but just be mindful of that terminology.
cues.zh: 當然，人生中還有比把零相關叫作沒有相關更嚴重的錯誤，但請留意這個用語。

cues.en: Now here is an interesting case over here.
cues.zh: 這裡有個有趣的情況。

cues.en: I'm gonna show you an example of two variables that have zero correlation.
cues.zh: 我要示範兩個零相關的變數。

cues.en: The correlation coefficient between variable x and variable y is zero.
cues.zh: 變數 X 與變數 Y 之間的相關係數為 0。

cues.en: Here it is.
cues.zh: 就是這個。

cues.en: Now this may seem surprising because I said that zero correlation means that there is no relationship between the two variables.
cues.zh: 這可能讓人驚訝，因為我剛才說，零相關表示兩個變數沒有關係。

cues.en: And that seems inconsistent with what you see here because there's clearly a very strong relationship between these two variables.
cues.zh: 但這似乎與眼前的圖不一致，因為這兩個變數顯然有非常強的關係。

cues.en: However, keep in mind that a correlation coefficient measures only a linear relationship between two variables.
cues.zh: 不過請記住，相關係數只衡量兩個變數之間的線性關係。

cues.en: And it turns out that in this case, with a circle distribution like this, there is no linear relationship between these two variables.
cues.zh: 像這種圓形分布，兩個變數之間恰好沒有線性關係。

cues.en: There is a non-linear relationship, a very, very strong non-linear relationship.
cues.zh: 它們有非線性關係，而且是非常強的非線性關係。

cues.en: But there is no linear relationship between these two variables.
cues.zh: 但兩個變數之間沒有線性關係。

cues.en: There isn't a clear line that you could draw through here that would give you something that looks like this.
cues.zh: 你無法在這裡畫一條清楚的直線，讓它看起來像這樣。

cues.en: So it's not the case that when one variable goes up, the other variable goes up or goes down.
cues.zh: 它不是一個變數上升，另一個變數就上升或下降的情況。

cues.en: So that means that you can have a zero correlation coefficient between two variables, and those variables can still be strongly related to each other.
cues.zh: 因此，兩個變數的相關係數可以為 0，但它們彼此仍然有很強的關係。

cues.en: They can be strongly dependent on each other, but that would have to be a non-linear relationship.
cues.zh: 它們可以非常相依，但那必須是一種非線性關係。

cues.en: Okay, so this is about positive correlations, negative correlations, zero correlations.
cues.zh: 以上是正相關、負相關與零相關。

cues.en: And now what I wanna show you is a few examples of different correlation strengths.
cues.zh: 接著要示範幾種不同的相關強度。

cues.en: So here we have r equals one.
cues.zh: 這裡 r 等於 1。

cues.en: So these are two variables, x and y, and they are perfectly correlated.
cues.zh: 這是 X 與 Y 兩個變數，它們完全相關。

cues.en: That's what we say when the correlation coefficient is one, perfectly correlated with each other.
cues.zh: 相關係數為 1 時，我們就說兩者完全相關。

cues.en: All of the dots lie on exactly one line.
cues.zh: 所有點都精確落在同一條直線上。

cues.en: Here is a case where we have a positive correlation, so 0.75, still a pretty robust correlation and the p-value is much less than 0.05.
cues.zh: 這裡是正相關，值為 0.75，仍然是相當強的相關，而且 P 值遠小於 0.05。

cues.en: So this is definitely a statistically significant correlation.
cues.zh: 因此這肯定是統計顯著的相關。

cues.en: It's significantly different from a correlation of zero.
cues.zh: 它與零相關之間有顯著差異。

cues.en: And you can see that, well they don't all lie exactly on a line, but it's a clear linear relationship.
cues.zh: 可以看到，雖然所有點並非精確落在一條線上，但線性關係很明顯。

cues.en: It's not perfect.
cues.zh: 它並不完美。

cues.en: There's some variability in here that is not explained by the linear relationship.
cues.zh: 其中還有一些變異，無法用這個線性關係解釋。

cues.en: Now whether that's just noise or whether there's other differences between these two variables that we're not capturing in our experiment, all these are possible,
cues.zh: 可能只是雜訊，也可能是兩個變數之間還有其他差異，沒有被實驗捕捉到。這些都有可能，

cues.en: but we do see that there is a significant positive relationship between them.
cues.zh: 但我們確實看到兩者有顯著的正向關係。

cues.en: Okay, and here we have, now this is a little bit confusing at first because when you first look at this correlation or this cloud of dots,
cues.zh: 好，這裡的情況一開始有點容易混淆，因為第一次看這個相關，或這團資料點時，

cues.en: it might not seem like there's a real correlation here.
cues.zh: 你可能覺得這裡沒有真正的相關。

cues.en: It might look like these two variables are uncorrelated with each other, like they have a close to zero correlation, but the correlation coefficient
cues.zh: 這兩個變數看起來可能互不相關，也就是相關接近 0；但相關係數

cues.en: is actually 0.38 and the p-value is 0.04, so it's less than 0.05.
So we would consider this to be a statistically significant correlation coefficient.
cues.zh: 因此，我們會認為這是統計顯著的相關係數。

cues.en: So you can get a significant correlation between two variables, even if it's visually not super duper compelling, like this one or this one.
cues.zh: 所以，兩個變數可以有顯著相關，即使視覺上不像這個或這個例子那樣非常有說服力。

cues.en: And that's something to keep in mind.
cues.zh: 這一點要記住。

cues.en: It's important to visualize your data so you also get a sense of what the strength of the relationship looks like between the two variables, and not just blindly trust whatever number this is
cues.zh: 把資料視覺化很重要，才能掌握兩個變數的關係強度看起來如何，而不是盲目相信分析產生的

cues.en: and whatever p-value comes out from your analysis.
cues.zh: 任何數字與 P 值。

cues.en: Now, the p-value for the correlation coefficient is related both to the strength of the relationship, the tightness of this relationship around the best fit line, and it's also related to the number of sample points.
cues.zh: 相關係數的 P 值，既與關係強度，也就是資料在最佳擬合線周圍的緊密程度有關，也與樣本點數量有關。

cues.en: So you can have a fairly modest correlation or even a weak correlation.
cues.zh: 因此，你可以有相當普通，甚至很弱的相關。

cues.en: And if you have a really large sample size, the p-value is gonna get really small.
cues.zh: 但如果樣本數非常大，P 值就會變得非常小。

cues.en: You will see more examples of that later on in this section.
cues.zh: 本單元稍後還會看到更多例子。

cues.en: The final point that I want to touch on in this video is the distinction between correlation and causation.
cues.zh: 這支影片最後要談的是相關與因果之間的區別。

cues.en: And it's pretty easy.
cues.zh: 很簡單。

cues.en: Correlation is not the same thing as causation.
cues.zh: 相關與因果並不相同。

cues.en: Correlation does not imply or require causation.
cues.zh: 相關並不代表因果，也不需要因果關係。

cues.en: So a correlation merely shows a relationship.
cues.zh: 相關僅僅呈現一種關係。

cues.en: It does not reveal causality, it does not imply causality.
cues.zh: 它不會揭露因果，也不意味著因果。

cues.en: If you want to demonstrate causality, you have to do this using experimental manipulations.
cues.zh: 若要證明因果，就必須透過實驗操弄。

cues.en: There are experimental tools to introduce causality into your experiment and determine whether a correlation is reflecting a causal relationship.
cues.zh: 有些實驗工具，可以在實驗中引入因果，判定相關是否反映因果關係。

cues.en: However, just observing a correlation on its own is not an indicator of causality.
cues.zh: 然而，光是觀察到相關，本身並不是因果的指標。

cues.en: Here's an example, it's a fun example.
cues.zh: 這裡有個有趣的例子。

cues.en: And so it turns out that there's a correlation between the amount of ice cream that's consumed and the number of people who are attacked by sharks.
cues.zh: 冰淇淋的消費量，與遭到鯊魚攻擊的人數之間，竟然有相關。

cues.en: Now this shouldn't make any sense.
cues.zh: 這應該很不合理。

cues.en: Why is it that when people eat more ice cream sharks get more aggressive and start eating more people?
cues.zh: 為什麼人們多吃冰淇淋，鯊魚就變得更有攻擊性，開始吃更多人？

cues.en: It doesn't even have to be the same people who are eating ice cream and getting attacked by the shark.
cues.zh: 吃冰淇淋與被鯊魚攻擊的，甚至不必是同一群人。

cues.en: It's not like the shark is going for the ice cream and he's killing you to get to it.
cues.zh: 並不是鯊魚想吃冰淇淋，為了搶冰淇淋才把你殺了。

cues.en: It can be totally different groups of people who are eating more ice cream compared to the people who are getting attacked by sharks.
cues.zh: 吃更多冰淇淋的，與被鯊魚攻擊的，可以是完全不同的兩群人。

cues.en: So obviously a causal relationship does not make sense.
cues.zh: 所以，因果關係顯然不合理。

cues.en: So what is going on here?
cues.zh: 那究竟發生什麼事？

cues.en: Can you think of a reason why ice cream cone consumption or ice cream consumption and shark attacks are correlated with each other?
cues.zh: 你能想出為什麼冰淇淋甜筒消費量，或冰淇淋消費量，與鯊魚攻擊彼此相關嗎？

cues.en: Well, it has to do with the weather.
cues.zh: 這與天氣有關。

cues.en: When it's summertime, people go out more and they eat more ice cream and they're at the beach more.
cues.zh: 夏天時，人們更常外出，吃更多冰淇淋，也更常去海邊。

cues.en: They're in the ocean more.
cues.zh: 他們更常下海。

cues.en: So there's going to be more people in the ocean.
cues.zh: 所以海裡的人會更多。

cues.en: So there's a higher chance of getting attacked by sharks.
cues.zh: 遭到鯊魚攻擊的機率也就較高。

cues.en: So in this case, in this example, there is a third variable that is related to both of these, which is that it's summer.
cues.zh: 這個例子有一個同時與兩者相關的第三變數，也就是夏季。

cues.en: So it's the weather out and that's causing people to eat more ice cream, it's causing people to go into the ocean more, and that in turn increases the possibility
cues.zh: 天氣讓人多吃冰淇淋，也讓人更常下海，進而提高

cues.en: of getting bitten by a shark.
cues.zh: 被鯊魚咬傷的可能性。

cues.en: Okay, so a bit of a silly example, but it does drive the point home that a correlation doesn't say anything about causation.
cues.zh: 好，這個例子有點傻，但確實清楚說明了：相關無法告訴我們任何因果關係。

cues.en: Causation has to be determined only by experimental manipulations.
cues.zh: 因果只能透過實驗操弄來判定。

cues.en: Correlations can be found in any kind of data, even without any experimental manipulations.
cues.zh: 任何資料中都可以找到相關，即使沒有任何實驗操弄。

cues.en: Alright, so in this video I introduced you to correlation coefficients and what they do and do not show.
cues.zh: 這支影片介紹了相關係數，以及它能呈現與不能呈現的內容。

cues.en: In the next several videos, I'm gonna start making all this stuff be more rigorous, more precise with formulas and exact definitions of the different kinds of correlation coefficients
cues.zh: 接下來幾支影片會透過公式，以及各種相關係數的精確定義，讓這些內容更加嚴謹，

cues.en: and their associated statistical significances.
cues.zh: 並說明它們對應的統計顯著性。
